The U.S. Forest Service has vast holdings of commercial timberlands in Alaska and it vigorouply seeks more at present under provisions of the recently passed Native Claims Act.
This same memo similarly mentions no dates for designation of use/no use lands. It merely asks for submissions of administrative guidelines after May 1.
EOl1644 refers specifically in its preamble to recreation vehicles. Section 1 of that EO, and all subsequent sections thereafter, refer to ORVs with no specification of recreational vehicles whatsoever. Sec. 2 (3) defines ORV as any motorized vehicle capable of crosscountry travel; EOl1644 however makes these exceptions: registered motorboats, military, fire, law enforcement and emergency vehicles in use for those purposes, and any vehicle used with express authorization by permit, lease, license or contract. Interior's May 5 Kl4 Memo adds these exceptions: farm vehicles and other agricultural vehicles thusly used, vehicles used for harvest and transport of forest products, earthmoving and other construction equipment thusly used, golf carts, lawn mowers, garden tractors and snowblowers.
Therefore, recreation vehicles seems to be the only designation for those ORVs which EOll644 appears to deal with, as well as those conmercial and non-commercial ORVs (and military vehicles) when in use for non-military or non-commercial uses.
